measurementsAndInterpretations: Larissa shows deep broad 3-micron OH absorption and a sharp 2.72-micron feature after continuum removal and division by Proteus spectrum; Mg-bearing serpentine-like phyllosilicate identification is a laboratory spectral interpretation, not a mapped local fraction.
No clear water-ice or CO2 signature reported for Larissa; nondetection does not prove absolute absence. Proteus weak CO2 and weaker/absent 2.72 feature remain separate.
Ceres, Bennu and chondrite spectral comparisons are not Larissa image skins or identical chemistry claims.

Prolonged aqueous alteration, differentiated parent interiors, destruction during Triton capture versus tidal disruption and reaccretion are origin interpretations; no directly observed history, present ocean, plume or biology.
Unresolved spectra cannot register Voyager pixels or independently calibrate visible colour, terrain, observer lighting or local materials.

Neptune scattered light and extraction choices particularly affect below 1.7 and above 4.5 microns; solar analog program1128 and background reduction are spectral calibration methods, not scene photometry.
Figure S1 infrared wavelength slices and calculated ring overlays are not resolved visible Larissa geography. Product extraction, final licence and Voyager crosswalk remain open.
